class.name: TerrainMaterial3D
class.brief_description: A ground material built from geology, erosion detail, grass tint, wetness and snow.
class.description: A material that writes its own shader. It picks among five [TerrainMaterialLayer]s per pixel: bare rock, scree, soil, alluvium and beach sand. With a [TerrainGenerator3D] (see [method use_generator]) the choice follows the generator's geology maps; without one, rock takes slopes past [member rock_slope] and soil the rest. Layers meet by height blending (Mishkinis 2013). Past [member cliff_slope] textures are mapped biplanar (Quilez 2020) so cliffs do not stretch. Over the layers come the generator's erosion detail normal, the [GrassField3D] ground tint, the [WeatherMap3D]'s wetness and the [SnowCover3D] snowpack, using the same shader code as [BaseMaterial3D] (see [method BaseMaterial3D.get_snow_shader_code]), so snow and wet ground look the same on the terrain as on every other surface, rasterized or path traced.

method.name: get_layer
method.description: Returns the layer for a surface, or [code]null[/code] for the default.

method.name: get_shader_code
method.description: Returns the shader code the material writes for its current settings.

method.name: set_ground_cover
method.description: Small stones drawn as part of the ground past where real ones stop (set by [RockField3D], see [member RockField3D.ground_detail_cover]). [param near] and [param far] are cover maps over [param near_rect] and [param far_rect] (world X and Z, in metres); [param reach], [param band] and [param size] are the pebbles', gravel's and fine gravel's reach from the camera, the band they hand over in and their mean size; [param colors] the rock types' linear albedo. Single grains are drawn while a pixel covers under about a third of one, their mean once it covers more than one. [code]null[/code] maps turn it off.

method.name: set_layer
method.description: Sets the layer for a surface. [code]null[/code] uses a plain default.

method.name: update_shader
method.description: Writes the shader again. Setters that change the code call it themselves.

method.name: use_generator
method.description: Takes [member sea_level] and the erosion detail code from a [TerrainGenerator3D] that has generated. The geology maps reach the shader through the generator's global uniforms.

members.member: Log10 of the drainage area (m²) past which soil turns to alluvium.
River sediment along valley floors.

Height above [member sea_level] that sand reaches when there is no generator geology. With [member geology_enabled] and a [TerrainGenerator3D], sand follows the generator's beaches instead (and covers ground under the sea), so a low coastal plain behind a beach keeps its soil.
Height-blend transition depth. Smaller gives sharper borders between layers.
Slope in degrees past which textures are mapped biplanar.
Shader code that defines [code]terrain_detail_normal()[/code], usually [method TerrainGenerator3D.get_detail_shader_code]. Empty: no erosion detail.
Octaves of the erosion detail normal. It fades out where a pixel covers it.

If [code]true[/code], far ground takes the plant cover's colour from the cover map a [VegetationField3D] publishes, taking over from the near grass tint between [member far_start] and [member far_start] + [member far_fade]. Without a field publishing the cover map it does nothing.
Distance in metres over which the far blend takes over.

Distance (m) from the camera where the far sun shadows start to fade in, full at twice it: the ground's own horizon toward the sun ([member TerrainGenerator3D.sun_shadows]) shades it where the shadow cascades thin out and end, with a soft edge of the sun's half degree. Raster only (the path tracer traces the hills' shadows); needs [member sky_occlusion_enabled]. 0 switches them off.
Distance from the camera in metres where the far blend starts.

If [code]true[/code], the far blend ends where a streaming [VegetationField3D]'s placed plants end (the global shader parameter [code]vegetation_near_radius[/code]): it starts at that radius less [member far_fade]. With no field streaming it uses [member far_start].

If [code]true[/code], ledges of a [Landscape3D]'s [member Landscape3D.cliff_relief] shadow each other per pixel under the first directional light: a short march toward the sun through the same relief that bends the faces' normals. The shadow map holds the ledges only near the camera and too coarsely for half-metre steps; the march keeps their shadow lines sharp at any distance where the relief is wider than a pixel. Forward+ and Mobile; the path tracer traces the real shadows instead.
Follow the generator's geology maps when they are set.
Tint the ground where [GrassField3D] grows, as [method GrassField3D.get_ground_shader_code] does.

Take prints from a [GroundSurface3D] whose [member GroundSurface3D.material] is this material: the terrain sinks under the printed patch and freshly turned ground darkens (see [method BaseMaterial3D.get_ground_deform_shader_code]).

If [code]true[/code], steep faces and scree get rock detail without textures: a height from 3D noise (joints, beds, pits) and scree stones over a gravel and fines matrix, turned into a normal by its surface gradient and filtered by the pixel's footprint so it does not alias. [member rock_detail_scale] sets its size.
Bare rock.
Slope in degrees past which rock shows when there is no geology. With the generator's geology, rock follows its maps, and faces past [member cliff_slope] are bare too.
Beach sand.

If [code]true[/code], the sand varies in colour at the dune field's scale: redder where grains have lain longer (iron-oxide coats, patchy over hundreds of metres, strongest on thin stable sand), a coarser, darker lag on flat interdune floors, and paler, finer sand on slip faces at the angle of repose. The depth terms need a [TerrainGenerator3D] with dunes or a sand sea ([method TerrainGenerator3D.get_sand_depth_at]); the slip faces show on any sand. The same lines as [member GroundSurface3D.dune_tone], so the two meet without a seam.

If [code]true[/code], the coarse lag on thin, flat interdune sand (the [member sand_dune_tone]'s dark flats) carries granule ripples: long, low ripples about 1.2 m apart and up to 5 cm high, broad crests of darker coarse grains running across the generator's dune-building wind ([member TerrainGenerator3D.sand_sea_wind_angle]), drawn as a normal and tint; where a pixel spans several crests it takes their mean tone. The same lines as [member GroundSurface3D.granule_ripples].

Metres from the camera inside which the scree draws no stones of its own (parallax blocks, their normal and tone), only their bed of gravel and fines, because real stones lie there (RockField3D's scree layer out to its radius). The shader's stones fade in over the last fifth. 0: shader stones everywhere.
Loose rock below cliffs.
Height of the sea, the base of the beach band.
How much of the ground's sky occlusion applies, 0 to 1.

Raster only: the ground's ambient light comes from the sky its surface sees ([member TerrainGenerator3D.sky_occlusion]): ambient occlusion is the irradiance of that sky over the whole sky's, on the shading normal, from the harmonics in the [code]terrain_sky_map[/code] global. Without it, a slope under higher ground takes light from the whole sky, such as a low sunset glow the hills hide. The path tracer ignores it.
Lay the [SnowCover3D] snowpack over the ground.
Slope in degrees past which snow slides off (see [member BaseMaterial3D.snow_max_slope]).
Soil on gentle ground.
Darken and smooth the ground where the [WeatherMap3D] says it is wet, by each layer's [member TerrainMaterialLayer.porosity].
